conceptZh: 廚師動物的麵團夾住四隻小鴨，第四隻衝進方框裡，剛好變成「四」。
object: rotund chef animal, four rubber ducks
morph: a square 囗 with two legs inside
creativeAngle: 主角自信滿滿卻不準，小鴨自己跑進位置。
promptEn: Create an exactly 8-second animated comedy, locked frontal camera. Setting: a pale-pink kitchen backdrop with a cream counter; the glyph is bold ocean-blue 四, a square 囗 with a small 儿 shape inside. A rotund cartoon chef bear in a tall hat stands at left. The Traditional Chinese glyph 四 stays centered and uncropped at about 70% of frame height with generous margins. Moment one (0.0-1.8s): the chef flings a round of dough toward the counter, missing wildly; the first 四 is spoken as the dough hits the wall. Moment two (1.8-3.5s): three small rubber ducks waddle in, and the fourth sprints through the square frame, sliding the two legs into place; the second 四 is spoken as the frame snaps shut around them. Moment three (3.5-5.0s): four ducks line up in a tiny row in front of four spring flower pots, then sit under a toy sun and a snowflake; 四季 is spoken as the ducks pop up in turn. From 5.0-8.0s the glyph 四 is perfectly still and unobstructed; the chef bows while the ducks wiggle their tails; the glyph is still. Audio: one warm, friendly off-screen voice speaks slowly and distinctly in Taiwan-standard Mandarin, reading exactly these syllables with clear tones and no erhua: 「四、四、四季」 (ㄙˋ、ㄙˋ、ㄙˋ ㄐㄧˋ). Timing: first utterance at about 0.5s, second at about 2.5s, the word at about 4.4s; then stop, no repeats and no extra speech. Beneath the voice only quacks and soft flour puffs, no music. The single glyph is the only on-screen text; the vocabulary stays audio-only with no subtitles, watermark, clutter or flashing.

conceptZh: 橡膠恐龍手太短拿不了枕頭，只好套上方形充氣圈用肚子跟玩具機器人相撲對決；兩個都揮空轉圈，額頭「咚」一聲撞在一起，方形圈掉下來變成「囗」，機器人的兩根泡棉棒掉進框裡變成「儿」，合起來剛好是「四」。
object: a square inflatable belly-bumper ring worn by the rubber dinosaur, plus the toy robot's two foam duel sticks (one short straight, one long with a bent hooked tip)
morph: on the head BONK the square ring pops off the dinosaur and lands flat as the outer box 囗 of 四, and the robot's two dropped foam sticks tumble inside it as the short left slanting stroke and the right vertical-bend stroke (the 儿 shape), completing 四
creativeAngle: 上一版是靜態鴨子排隊、廚師丟麵團，沒有真正的身體搞笑。這一版改成「友誼對決」：恐龍因為手太短根本拿不到枕頭，只好整隻跳進方形充氣圈用肚子撞，機器人則用長短不一的手臂亂揮泡棉棒；兩人都揮空、原地轉圈、最後額頭相撞，撞擊本身把道具甩成「四」。選 四方形 是因為它可以直接用畫面呈現——「四」的外框本身就是四方形，機器人在旁邊用手臂在空中畫一個方形，聽到和看到是同一件事；方、形都只有一種讀音，發音安全。
promptEn:
Create an exactly 8-second 2D-style animated slapstick clip, locked frontal camera, bright soft-lit toy-room floor in pale butter yellow with a plain cream wall behind; nothing busy in the background. Only two characters on screen. LEAD: an original squishy rubber dinosaur, round green body, enormous flat feet, and comically tiny arms that cannot reach anything, so it does everything with its whole body. RIVAL: an original boxy toy robot built from mismatched parts, one arm noticeably longer than the other, motors that always run a little too strong. The teaching subject is the Traditional Chinese glyph 四, formed from solid saturated cobalt-blue props against the light floor: an outer square box 囗 (left vertical stroke, top horizontal bending down into the right vertical, bottom horizontal closing it) with, inside, a short left slanting stroke and a right vertical stroke that bends into a hook at the bottom, together reading like 儿 inside the box. The finished 四 is centered, uncropped, about 70% of frame height with clear margins, and is the only text in the clip.

Moment one, WANT IT (0.0-1.5s): the dinosaur at frame left spots the robot at frame right, who is proudly brandishing two cobalt-blue foam duel sticks, a short straight one in its short arm and a long bent-tip one in its long arm, swishing them with too much motor power. The dinosaur tries to pick up a pillow, tiny arms flapping uselessly a hand-width above it; it huffs, then flops belly-first into a cobalt-blue square inflatable bumper ring lying on the floor and pops up wearing it around its middle like a sumo belt, stomping its giant feet with a determined grin. The first 四 is spoken at about 0.6s as the dinosaur bounces up inside the square ring.

Moment two, TRY AND MISS (1.5-3.2s): the robot charges with a giant windmill wind-up of its long arm; the foam stick whiffs clean over the dinosaur's ducked head and the robot spins two full turns from its own momentum, eyes going swirly. The dinosaur answers with a belly-bump charge, square ring first, overshoots completely, skids on its huge feet past the robot and spins around too. A quick frozen beat: both face each other, panting, noses nearly touching.

Moment three, THE BIG BONK (3.2-4.6s): both lunge at the same instant and bump foreheads with a cartoon BOINK, big squash-and-stretch, little stars circling. The impact pops the square ring straight up off the dinosaur; it flips once and lands flat and perfectly centered as the box 囗 of 四. The robot's two foam sticks fly out of its hands and drop neatly inside the box, the short straight one landing as the left slanting stroke and the long bent-tip one as the right vertical-bend stroke, completing a correctly formed 四. The second 四 is spoken at about 3.9s exactly as the sticks click into place. Both characters sit down dazed on either side of the glyph, well clear of the strokes.

Moment four, PAYOFF (4.6-8.0s): from 4.6s the glyph 四 stays perfectly still, centered and unobstructed. The robot, sitting at lower right, raises its long arm and draws a glowing square shape in the air beside itself, tapping each of its four corners with a soft blink; the word 四方形 is spoken at about 5.0s as that square is traced, with the dinosaur nodding and pointing with its whole head toward the matching square box of the glyph. Then the dinosaur waddles over to the robot in the lower-right corner, tries to shake hands, tiny arm hopelessly short, gives up and offers one enormous foot instead; the robot shakes the foot with its long arm, both grinning and wobbling, never touching or covering the strokes. The glyph remains clearly readable for the full final 3 seconds.

Audio: one warm, friendly off-screen voice speaks slowly and distinctly in clear Taiwan-standard Mandarin, reading exactly these syllables with clear tones, no erhua and no neutral-tone shortcuts: 「四、四、四方形」 (ㄙˋ、ㄙˋ、ㄙˋ ㄈㄤ ㄒㄧㄥˊ). First utterance at about 0.6s, second at about 3.9s, the word at about 5.0s; then stop, no repeats, no extra speech. Under the voice only soft rubber squeaks, little motor whirs, a gentle cartoon BOINK and foam thuds; no music louder than the voice. No subtitles, no vocabulary text, no watermark, no clutter, no flashing; bright but not neon, no white blowouts, no dark grading.
